claims.text: The material of interest is a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a conventional metal substrate.
Overall wear resistance at high temperature is governed by formation of a stable, single-phase solid solution.
Microscopic deformation during sliding at high temperature is governed by formation of a stable, single-phase solid solution.
Changing the coating composition will alter its entropy of mixing.
The FeNiCrCoCu coating forms a stable, single-phase solid solution in the intended high-temperature regime.
Increasing entropy of mixing stabilizes the single-phase solid solution.
A stabilized single-phase solid solution reduces microscopic deformation.
A stabilized single-phase solid solution improves wear resistance.
Increasing entropy of mixing will decrease the coating's wear rate.
Increasing entropy of mixing will decrease microscopic deformation.
The directional predictions are intended to hold in a high-temperature operating regime.
Single-phase solid solutions can be produced in at least some high-entropy alloys.
High-entropy alloys are relevant to high-temperature applications.

contradictions.description: The intervention and prediction require comparison among coating compositions with different entropies of mixing, but the stated baseline is an uncoated substrate, for which coating composition and coating entropy of mixing are undefined.
